summary.text: Dave Seeman of Nashville, an independent endorsed by the Green Party of Tennessee who qualified by petition, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Governor of Tennessee to Marsha Blackburn.
An engineer and business owner who co-founded a product design firm, he made his first run for office after working as a climate activist.
His campaign centered on a policy document he called The Volunteer Plan.

paragraphs.text: Seeman grew up in Franklin and lives in Nashville.

He earned a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, and spent most of his career at the product design firm he co-founded, which he says became an award-winning firm that kept its employees on with benefits through COVID.
Before running for office he was a climate activist who lobbied other candidates to make climate action central to their campaigns.
Seeman filed his petition from Nashville on March 9, 2026, and the Secretary of State recorded its signatures as approved.
He says he built The Volunteer Plan the way he designed medical devices, by interviewing Tennesseans and compiling data into a costed, budget-balanced package of policies.
Its education proposals included repealing the Education Freedom Scholarship program and redirecting $144 million a year into public schools.
Seeman described his campaign as "no party, no pacs, just an engineer building better government, by design."
He received 870 votes, less than 0.1% of the vote, to Marsha Blackburn's 45.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
